def BytesIOCopy(copy_to: t.BinaryIO) -> t.BinaryIO:
    """Return a binary stream that copies everything written to it into
    ``copy_to``.

    Unlike ``io.BytesIO``, the returned stream is backed by a real OS file
    descriptor, so it can be used as ``stdout``/``stderr`` for a
    :class:`subprocess.Popen` (e.g. via :func:`subprocess.run`) invoked by
    code under test.

    .. versionadded:: 8.2

    .. versionchanged:: 8.3.3
        Backed by a real file instead of :class:`io.BytesIO` so that
        ``fileno()`` is available to subprocesses.
        :issue:`2523`
    """
    stream = tempfile.TemporaryFile()
    raw_write = stream.write
    raw_flush = stream.flush

    def write(b: ReadableBuffer) -> int:
        copy_to.write(b)
        return raw_write(b)

    def flush() -> None:
        raw_flush()
        copy_to.flush()

    def getvalue() -> bytes:
        pos = stream.tell()
        stream.seek(0)
        data = stream.read()
        stream.seek(pos)
        return data

    stream.write = write  # type: ignore[method-assign]
    stream.flush = flush  # type: ignore[method-assign]
    stream.getvalue = getvalue  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    return t.cast("t.BinaryIO", stream)

class BytesIOCopy:
    """A binary stream, backed by a real (temporary) file so that it has a
    usable ``fileno()``, that copies everything written to it into another
    stream.

    Being backed by a real file (rather than :class:`io.BytesIO`) allows the
    stream to be passed to APIs such as :func:`subprocess.run` that need a
    file descriptor, for example when a command redirects its own
    `<stdout>`/`<stderr>` to a subprocess.

    .. versionadded:: 8.2

    .. versionchanged:: 8.3
        Backed by a temporary file instead of :class:`io.BytesIO` so
        ``fileno()`` is supported.
    """

    def __init__(self, copy_to: t.BinaryIO | None = None) -> None:
        self._file = tempfile.TemporaryFile()
        self.copy_to = copy_to

    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> t.Any:
        return getattr(self._file, name)

    def write(self, b: ReadableBuffer) -> int:
        if self.copy_to is not None:
            self.copy_to.write(b)
        return self._file.write(b)

    def flush(self) -> None:
        self._file.flush()
        if self.copy_to is not None:
            self.copy_to.flush()

    def getvalue(self) -> bytes:
        pos = self._file.tell()
        self._file.seek(0)
        data = self._file.read()
        self._file.seek(pos)
        return data


class StreamMixer:
    """Mixes `<stdout>` and `<stderr>` streams.

    The result is available in the ``output`` attribute.

    .. versionadded:: 8.2
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.output: BytesIOCopy = BytesIOCopy()
        self.stdout: BytesIOCopy = BytesIOCopy(copy_to=self.output)
        self.stderr: BytesIOCopy = BytesIOCopy(copy_to=self.output)
